title: A smooth fibre neighbourhood gives smoothness of its affine fibre ring at the kernel prime
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$, and $s=f(x)$. Let $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ be affine open neighbourhoods of $x$ and $s$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $f(W)\subseteq V$, and let $\varphi:R\to A$ be the induced ring map. Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ represent $x$ and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Set $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=A\otimes_R k$, with $k\to F$ given by $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\rho:F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ send $a\otimes\lambda$ to $\bar a\bar\lambda$, using the residue-field map induced by $\varphi$, and put $\mathfrak Q=\ker\rho$. Suppose the fibre morphism $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field] is smooth on an open neighbourhood of its unique point above $x$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $k\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: there exists $h\in F\setminus\mathfrak Q$ for which $k\to F_h$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, proof of (2) implies (1): affine translation of the smooth-fibre hypothesis before applying Algebra lemma-flat-fibre-smooth.

proof.text: Identify $\kappa(s)$ with $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\kappa(x)$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Indeed, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (b),(c) identifies the ambient stalks, including their germ maps from $R,A$, with the corresponding affine stalks and prime localizations; quotienting these local-ring isomorphisms by their maximal ideals gives the residue-field identifications. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (2), the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ factors through $V$ and corresponds on $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ to the residue map of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak p$; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] this map is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to k)$ after the identification $\kappa(s)=k$. Hence the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ is the composite of $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to k)$ with $V\hookrightarrow S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality] (2), the scheme residue-field map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ becomes exactly the field map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ induced by $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6); Tag 01HY, lemma-morphism-into-affine-where-point-goes; affine residue-field comparison in the proof of Morphisms Tag 01V9.

proof.text: Write $\pi:X_s\to X$ for the fibre projection [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to $X\to S$, $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$, and the opens $W\subset X$, $V\subset S$, and all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its hypotheses hold because $f(W)\subset V$ and the second map factors through $V$ by step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $f\circ\iota_W=\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for the canonical open immersions $\iota_W:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$, so the restriction $W\to V$ of $f$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ under these identifications. It identifies $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}k$ with the open subscheme $\pi^{-1}(W)$ of $X_s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] this gives an isomorphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}F\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^{-1}(W)$, with projection to $W$ induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ induced by $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$. This computation needs no finite-presentation hypothesis on $A$.

source.place: Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product; Tags 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, and 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affines.

proof.text: The formula for $\rho$ respects the tensor relation: for $r\in R$, the images of $\varphi(r)a\otimes\lambda$ and $a\otimes r\lambda$ both equal $\bar a\,\bar r\,\bar\lambda$. It is multiplicative and unital, hence its kernel $\mathfrak Q$ is prime because its codomain is a field. The unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ maps under $\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ to $\mathfrak Q$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality] (1) (the prime in this field is $(0)$). Its composite with the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is induced by $a\mapsto\bar a$ and therefore maps to $\mathfrak q$. Equivalently, $a\otimes1\in\mathfrak Q$ iff $a\in\mathfrak q$. Thus $j(\mathfrak Q)$ lies above $x$. The fibre projection is a homeomorphism onto $f^{-1}(s)$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre], so $j(\mathfrak Q)$ is precisely the unique fibre point $\xi$ above $x$.

source.place: Tag 01HY, lemma-morphism-into-affine-where-point-goes; Tag 01K1, lemma-fibre-topological; the tensor formula is checked directly.

proof.text: Let $N\subset X_s$ be the open neighbourhood of $\xi$ on which the fibre structure morphism is smooth. Under $j$, the intersection $N\cap\pi^{-1}(W)$ is an open $O\subset\operatorname{Spec}F$ containing $\mathfrak Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (i), choose $h\in F$ with $\mathfrak Q\in D(h)\subset O$; thus $h\notin\mathfrak Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}F_h\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ identifies its source with the open subscheme $D(h)$, with inclusion induced by $F\to F_h$. Restrict the smooth map $N\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ to this open subscheme and use the identifications of steps 1 and 2. Clauses (a) and (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] give a smooth morphism $\operatorname{Spec}F_h\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its ring map is explicitly $k\to F\to F_h$, $\lambda\mapsto(1\otimes\lambda)/1$, by the projection formula in step 2.

source.place: Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; Algebra Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology (basic-open basis); Morphisms Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize (restriction); More on Morphisms Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] to the ring homomorphism $k\to F_h$ from step 4: its spectrum morphism is smooth, so it is a smooth ring map. Together with $h\notin\mathfrak Q$, this is exactly smoothness of $k\to F$ at $\mathfrak Q$ as defined in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].
